newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq stocks find support at last, close higher.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq stocks find support at last, close higher.

text.p: Nasdaq stocks lurched higher on Thursday as technology shares ended a string of heavy losses despite a warning of potential interest rate hikes from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.
The Nasdaq Composite Index rose 9.97 points, or 0.8 percent, to an unofficial close of 1259.26.

"The techs were overdue for a bounce," said Brian Finnerty, managing director of trading at Unterberg Harris. "You've got to go through these shakeouts every now and then, even though they're gut-wrenching."

Intel was the most active share, down 1/8 to 133-1/4. Other technology issues rose, including Ascend Communications, which gained 4-1/2 to 50-1/4 after Dillon Read reiterated its buy rating and price target of 90.
Sun Microsystems rose 2-1/8 to 28-3/4 after a positive report on the outlook for network computers. Adaptec rose 3-15/16 to 37-3/8.
Greenspan appeared to warn a Congressional panel that the Fed could raise interest rates, possibly as soon as next Tuesday's meeting, analysts said.
Advancing issues led declining shares 2,081 to 1,915. Trading volume totaled 631 million shares.
